chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Dawud ibn Isa from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Abyssinian chicken (a type of fowl), so he said: 'It is not among the game; rather, the game is that which is between the sky and the earth.'

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'That which from the birds does not line up (in rows), you may take it out of the Sanctuary; and that which from them does line up, you may not take it out.'
And the cheetah and what resembles it from the beasts of prey, if a person brings it into the Sanctuary as a captive, there is no harm in taking it out from it. Narrated.

key_terms.الدَّجَّاجِ الْحَبَشِيِّ: Abyssinian chicken, a type of fowl
key_terms.يَصُفُّ: To line up in rows (referring to bird formation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting birds and animals inside the Haram sanctuary according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the definition of 'game' (sayd) for expiation by excluding Abyssinian chickens, which do not line up in flight, thereby distinguishing them from true wild birds. This narration highlights the juristic nuance in identifying permissible prey within the Haram boundaries, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of hunting sacrifices.
